summary.oneLiner: Arkade is an execution-first Mumbai (MMR) residential developer pivoting up the value curve into premium/luxury, funded by a mix of redevelopment rights and outright land buys. FY26 was a "defining year": record quarterly pre-sales (Rs. 303 cr in Q4, +40% YoY) and a marquee, optionality-heavy acquisition (Filmistan, Goregaon West) that anchors a Rs. 3,500 cr GDV uber-luxury project. The reported PAT (Rs. 5 cr FY26) is optically crushed by a one-time Rs. 182 cr non-cash diminution of Filmistan tenancy rights — operationally the business grew. Stated pipeline of ~Rs. 12,000 cr over 5–6 years with a launch-driven (Thane + Filmistan) inflection from FY28. Key debate raised by analysts: 25% CAGR alone only gets cumulative revenue to ~Rs. 5,000–6,000 cr over six years, so the thesis leans heavily on the big-ticket launches converting to "exponential" growth in FY28/FY29.

| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | YoY | FY26 | FY25 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-sales / bookings value | Rs. 303 cr (highest-ever qtr) | Rs. 217 cr | +40% | Rs. 901 cr | Rs. 773 cr | +17% |
| Area sold | 1,10,000 sq ft | 70,000 sq ft | +57% | 3,15,000 sq ft | 2,49,000 sq ft | +27% |
| Implied realization (value/area) | ~Rs. 27,500/sq ft | ~Rs. 31,000/sq ft | ↓ mix | ~Rs. 28,600/sq ft | ~Rs. 31,000/sq ft | ↓ mix |
| Collections | Rs. 195 cr | n/a | — | Rs. 728 cr | Rs. 716 cr | +2% |
| Reported revenue (POCS-noisy) | Rs. 199 cr | Rs. 134 cr | +48% | Rs. 828 cr | Rs. 695 cr | +19.2% |
| EBITDA | Rs. 38 cr | n/a | — | Rs. 189 cr | n/a | — |
| EBITDA margin | 19.4% | n/a | — | 23.2% | n/a | — |
| PAT | n/a | n/a | — | Rs. 5 cr (post one-off) | n/a | — |
| Net debt | "balance sheet remains healthy"; no figure given (mgmt frames as low-leverage / flexible) | | | | | |

**One-offs (explicit):** FY26 PAT includes a one-time exceptional non-cash item — diminution in value of Filmistan tenancy rights of **Rs. 182.17 cr** (per CFO Rs. ~183 cr acquisition cost written off on demerger order received Mar '26). This cost will *reduce the future project cost* of the Filmistan project (i.e., margin accretive later). Income-tax provision Rs. 2 cr. Note: realization/sq ft optically dipped YoY on product/stage mix, not pricing weakness (mgmt cites steady price appreciation in market).
guidance (critical — pre-sales, launches:
- **Revenue growth:** ~20–25% YoY for FY27 ("Rs. 1,200–1,300 cr next year" implied; mgmt says next year "should be more" due to Thane launch). **Exponential growth flagged for FY28 & FY29** once Filmistan + Thane contribute full-year.
- **Pipeline:** ~**Rs. 12,000 cr** (analyst referenced "12,700 cr") of projects spread over next **5–6 years**; full recognition targeted in **~6 years**.
- **Margins:** EBITDA margin expected to **stabilize at 27–28%** (MD said "targeting ~25%"); **PAT margin to stabilize ~18–19%**.
- **Launches:** Thane project to launch **this financial year (FY27)**; Filmistan uber-luxury project under approval, **launch targeted by FY-end (FY27)**.
- **Business development:** Just-signed MOU for **cluster redevelopment of 9 societies at Ashok Nagar, Kandivali East** — RERA carpet ~**3.25 lakh sq ft**, GDV ~**Rs. 1,100 cr**.
- **Near-term color:** May/Q1 pre-sales "consistent but a little slow" vs Q4 — attributed to war impact, fuel prices, global macro; mgmt notes Q4 seasonally always > Q1 in real estate.
pipeline (ongoing + upcoming gdv; land /:
- **Total pipeline ~Rs. 12,000 cr** GDV over 5–6 years.
- **Filmistan (Goregaon West, SV Road):** uber-luxury residential; GDV ~**Rs. 3,500 cr**; estimated cumulative bottom-line contribution **Rs. 1,000–1,200 cr over next 3–5 years**; under approval, launch by FY27-end. Land bought outright (Rs. 165 cr, paid Jan '25) + tenancy rights (~Rs. 182.6 cr) consolidated into Arkade.
- **Ashok Nagar, Kandivali East (NEW MOU this quarter):** 9-society cluster redevelopment; ~3.25 lakh sq ft RERA carpet; GDV ~**Rs. 1,100 cr**.
- **Thane project:** launching FY27 — flagged as the key near-term growth spike.
- Mgmt: two further "cluster redevelopment projects" cited alongside Thane/Filmistan as exponential-growth drivers.
segment: Single reportable theme: MMR residential. Mix shifting toward **premium/luxury** — luxury share of MMR sales (by area) climbed to **44% in 9M FY26 from 31% in FY21**; Rs. 2–5 cr ticket now dominates registrations; sub-Rs. 1 cr (affordable) shrinking. Arkade positioning itself in premium + luxury (Filmistan = uber-luxury benchmark).
growth / optionality:
- Redevelopment pipeline expanding via cluster deals (Ashok Nagar 9 societies; two more cluster projects referenced).
- New micro-markets / "center of gravity" expanding to Thane, Navi Mumbai, Mira Road — infra catalysts: Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link (MTHL), extended metro lines.
- Filmistan as a brand-defining flagship that re-rates the premium positioning; written-off tenancy cost lowers future project cost = embedded margin optionality.
- ~20% manpower added in front-ending Execution & Sales teams ahead of growth.
margins & cost:
- Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 19.4% (down sequentially per analyst); FY26 23.2%.
- Guided to stabilize **27–28% EBITDA / 18–19% PAT**.
- Filmistan tenancy write-off (Rs. 182 cr) will **reduce future Filmistan project cost**, supporting later-year margins.
- Reported revenue is POCS-driven and noisy vs the operational pre-sales metrics — focus on pre-sales/collections.
capex / project-starts:
- Filmistan land: Rs. 165 cr outright (paid Jan '25); tenancy ~Rs. 182.6 cr.
- Project-starts queued: Thane (FY27), Filmistan (FY27-end), Ashok Nagar cluster (post-MOU/approvals).
- No explicit standalone capex number; spend is project-acquisition + development driven.
capital allocation (net cash): - Balance sheet described as "healthy," providing flexibility for growth while "maintaining financial discipline" — net-debt figure NOT quantified on call. Funding model: redevelopment (low land outlay) + selective outright buys (Filmistan Rs. 165 cr cash). No buyback/dividend commentary.
risks:
- **Approvals risk:** Filmistan (Rs. 3,500 cr GDV) and Ashok Nagar still pre-launch / under approval — timeline slippage hits the FY28/FY29 "exponential" thesis.
- **MMR concentration:** 100% Mumbai-region exposure (Goregaon, Kandivali, Mira Road, Thane).
- **Demand softness:** mgmt flagged Q1/May slowdown from war, fuel prices, global macro.
- **Math gap:** analysts noted 25% CAGR alone only reaches ~Rs. 5,000–6,000 cr cumulative over 6 yrs vs Rs. 12,000 cr pipeline — execution/launch conversion is the swing factor.
- **Realization mix** drifting lower YoY (value/area) — watch product mix vs pricing.
management tone: Confident, execution-first, founder-led (Amit Jain). Candid on near-term softness ("not more than" Q4's 40% growth in Q1; macro headwinds named). CFO precise on margin/one-off mechanics. Repeated framing: "value creation comes from timely execution, customer trust," not just owning land.
non-obvious:
- The Rs. 182 cr write-off is the *reason* reported PAT collapsed to Rs. 5 cr — purely accounting/non-cash, and it lowers future Filmistan project cost (margin-positive later). Easy to misread as operational weakness.
- Filmistan structuring: outright land (Aspen/Kamanwala) + tenancy via Filmistan Pvt Ltd (WoS) → demerged/merged into Arkade (order Mar '26) to consolidate ownership.
- Ashok Nagar MOU signed literally the evening before the call ("last evening") — fresh pipeline add.
- Mgmt implicitly distinguishes EBITDA "targeting 25%" (MD) vs "stabilize 27–28%" (CFO) — a 2–3pt aspiration gap.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- MMR premiumization / luxury up-cycle (luxury 31%→44% of area) ✅ benefits premium-focused MMR developers incl. Arkade.
- Infra catalysts (MTHL, metro) ✅ lift peripheral MMR land values (Thane/Navi Mumbai/Mira Road developers). ⭐ none company-specific beyond Arkade itself.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Described as a "Leading MMR Developer with Inhouse Project Management", specialising in premium residential development across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region with a strategic focus on high-demand micro-markets.
- Value proposition rests on a diversified portfolio across greenfield and redevelopment projects, an asset-light model with low net debt, strong cash-flow and IRR focus, expansion in the Eastern Corridor and "Quick Turn around - Before Time Delivery".
- Snapshot claims a 40+ year legacy of excellence, 32 projects completed, 5,500+ homes delivered and 5.5 Mn Sq.Ft + area delivered; the completed portfolio slide splits the 32 projects into 18 greenfield and 14 redevelopment.
- Industry case for MMR: India's largest residential market by sales volume (97,188 units in 2025 vs 55,373 Bengaluru), infrastructure-led growth (metro, Navi Mumbai International Airport, Atal Setu/MTHL), and redevelopment at ~60-65% of Mumbai's residential development pipeline.
- Awards cited include Project of the Year (Arkade Earth), Iconic Residential Developer, and Iconic Luxury Residential Project of the Year (Arkade Aura); issuer rating IND-RA BBB+, ISO-9001-2015 and ISO-45001-2018 certified.

- Ashok Nagar MOU signed literally the evening before the call ("last evening") — fresh pipeline add.
- Mgmt implicitly distinguishes EBITDA "targeting 25%" (MD) vs "stabilize 27–28%" (CFO) — a 2–3pt aspiration gap.

challenges.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- MMR premiumization / luxury up-cycle (luxury 31%→44% of area) ✅ benefits premium-focused MMR developers incl. Arkade.
- Infra catalysts (MTHL, metro) ✅ lift peripheral MMR land values (Thane/Navi Mumbai/Mira Road developers). ⭐ none company-specific beyond Arkade itself.

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Record qtr pre-sales Rs. 303 cr (+40% YoY); area 1.10 lakh sq ft (+57%); FY26 pre-sales Rs. 901 cr (+17%), area 3.15 lakh sq ft (+27%); collections FY26 Rs. 728 cr. Rev Q4 Rs. 199 cr (+48%), FY26 Rs. 828 cr (+19.2%); EBITDA margin Q4 19.4% / FY26 23.2%; PAT Rs. 5 cr after Rs. 182 cr Filmistan tenancy write-off. NEW: Ashok Nagar 9-society cluster MOU (Rs. 1,100 cr GDV); Filmistan Rs. 3,500 cr GDV project under approval (launch FY27-end); Thane launch FY27. Pipeline ~Rs. 12,000 cr / 5–6 yrs. Guidance: FY27 +20–25%, exponential FY28/FY29; EBITDA stabilize 27–28%, PAT 18–19%.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [ESG/Certification] The deck cites ISO-9001-2015 and ISO-45001-2018 certification and promoter-family philanthropy through the Sajjan Jain Trust (education, healthcare, welfare), but sets out no sustainability, emissions or green-building targets.
- [Exceptional item] FY26 consolidated accounts carry an exceptional item of INR (1,822) Mn, which took FY26 PBT to INR 79 Mn and PAT to INR 53 Mn; the deck does not explain the nature of the exceptional item.
- [Shareholding] Promoter Group holds 71.19% and Public 28.81% as on 30th June 2026; 185.66 Mn equity shares outstanding, face value INR 10.
- [Governance] Board includes three promoter-family executive directors (Amit Mangilal Jain as Chairman & MD, Sandeep Jain and Arpit Jain as Whole-time Directors) alongside three independent directors chairing the Audit, Stakeholders' Relationship and Nomination & Remuneration Committees.
- [Business development] Successfully advanced business development through strategic land acquisitions across key MMR micro-markets; earlier journey milestones include the Filmistan Pvt Ltd acquisition (4-acre Goregaon, projected GDV Rs. 3,500 cr), Thane entry (Rs. 1,900 cr), a Bhandup 3.5-acre MOU (Rs. 1,000 cr) and rights to redevelop 13.5 acres in the western suburbs (Rs. 4,500 cr).
